articles.title: Newsom's bid to empty California's death row collides with voters' repeated rejection of abolition
articles.summary: A lawsuit challenges Democratic California Gov. Gavin Newsom's effort to commute all 548 death sentences, citing failures to notify district attorneys.
articles.body:
A lawsuit challenging Democratic California Gov. Gavin Newsom's plan to commute 548 death sentences is raising questions about the governor's clemency powers, with a legal expert arguing Newsom is using his gubernatorial authority to circumvent the will of voters who have repeatedly rejected efforts to abolish capital punishment.

Newsom announced Nov. 5 that he intends to commute the death sentences of all 548 inmates on the Golden State's death row to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole, a move that will take effect only after the necessary legal steps are completed.

The Criminal Justice Legal Foundation (CJLF) on Sunday filed a lawsuit at the California Supreme Court seeking to block Newsom's proposed sweeping commutation, citing the governor's "failure to provide legally required notice to district attorneys and his disregard for the rights of victims and their families to be notified and heard," according to a news release.

Newsom may be using clemency to impose his own views on capital punishment despite voters repeatedly rejecting abolition, Zack Smith, a senior legal fellow for Courts and the Constitution at the Heritage Foundation, told Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

"The death penalty remains on the books in California, and as you alluded to, California voters have repeatedly rejected efforts to abolish the death penalty," Smith said. "So Californians understand that it can be an appropriate punishment in certain circumstances. Now, [Gov.] Newsom, he does have the ability to exercise the pardon, the commutation power, the contours of that obviously are being litigated, but I think what's clear is that from a practical standpoint, [Gov.] Newsom is essentially using this to circumvent the clear will of the voters and impose his own views of the death penalty over those of ... the California populace."

"Now some of the specifics related to this suit challenging Gavin Newsom's use of the commutation pardon, that is going to vary a little bit from state to state," Smith added. "So this is going focus largely on issues of California state law and the issues specifically that I think will get the most attention is whether the California Supreme Court would essentially have to weigh in and more or less approve some of these repeat offenders before their sentences can be commuted."

California voters notably defeated Proposition 34 , a ballot initiative to ban capital punishment, in 2012, according to Ballotpedia. Voters in the Golden State similarly rejected Proposition 62, the Abolition of Death Penalty Measure , in November 2016, per Ballotpedia.

The lawsuit alleges that Newsom "has claimed to himself the unfettered power to decide how clemency should be granted, ignored the Legislature's requirement of a referral to the Board of Parole Hearings for investigation and recommendation, ignored the role of the trial court and District Attorney in providing crucial factual input to the Board of Parole Hearings, ignored the limitation of the required notice to District Attorneys, and deprived the Legislature, the public, and this Court of the information needed to determine whether he has abused his authority."

CJLF's lawsuit also requests that "the Court immediately stay any issuance, implementation, recognition, or enforcement of the challenged commutations pending further order of the Court and pending determination of this petition on the merits."

Anne Marie Schubert, president and CEO of CJLF, said in a statement that the lawsuit "is about protecting the constitutional rights of victims, defending the rule of law, and ensuring that no Governor is above the law."

"The Governor's clemency power does not authorize mass commutations that disregard constitutional safeguards, legally required procedures, or victims' rights," Schubert said, adding that "blanket commutation is not an exercise of discretion — it is an abandonment of it."

CJLF and Newsom's office did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

The coalition suing Newsom is comprised of several law enforcement leaders and organizations, victims' rights groups and multiple district attorneys, including Sacramento County District Attorney Thien Ho, who ran as a Democrat in the 2026 congressional primary.

Some of California's most notorious serial killers are among the death row inmates whose sentences Newsom plans to commute, KTLA reported Nov. 8.

"Obviously, these are individuals who, again, have been convicted by a jury of their peers of committing particularly aggravated forms of murder," Smith told Fox News Digital. "Again, many of these individuals tortured their victims and included sexual violence against their victims before they were ultimately killed. And so these are individuals that their own peers thought deserved the death penalty. And, so again, to see [Gov.] Newsom circumventing this through his commutation power is very, very troubling."

Under the California Constitution, Newsom must obtain a recommendation from at least four California Supreme Court justices before commuting the sentences of 382 inmates who have been convicted of more than one felony.

The California Supreme Court has invited interested parties to weigh in on the proposed commutations, with legal briefs due Nov. 24 and Newsom's response due Dec. 4. Attorney General Rob Bonta told the court Newsom will not formally commute any death sentences until the justices act, including those of inmates with only one felony conviction.

Newsom's office has argued that the governor's broad constitutional clemency authority allows him to initiate blanket commutations without following statutory procedures governing individual applications, while separately seeking the California Supreme Court's required recommendation for inmates with multiple felony convictions.

"District attorneys have a legal responsibility to represent the people of California and protect the rights of crime victims," Greg Totten, CEO of the California District Attorneys Association , said in a statement. "The Governor's failure to provide legally required notice to prosecutors has deprived them of the opportunity to provide critical information and ensure that victims and their families are heard."

"No Governor should be permitted to circumvent the very safeguards designed to ensure that justice is served," Totten added.

Newsom's proposed commutations would mark the largest mass commutation of death sentences in American history, according to the Death Penalty Information Center.

Newsom also issued a March 2019 executive order establishing a moratorium on executions in California, leaving the state's death penalty law and existing death sentences in place.

Democratic California Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra said in a May 28, 2026, X post that he plans to extend California's moratorium on executions when he takes office.

"Governor Newsom's death penalty moratorium represented an important step toward a more just criminal justice system," Becerra wrote in the post. "As Governor, I will extend California's moratorium on executions and continue moving our state away from a costly, flawed system that disproportionately impacts Black and brown communities and too often gets it wrong."

Dan Dow, district attorney of San Luis Obispo County, California, blasted Newsom's proposed commutation as "a sickening abuse of power" in a Nov. 5 statement.

"Governor Newsom just told the families of Rachel Newhouse, Aundria Crawford, Kesha Gurke and every other innocent victim of California's 548 condemned killers that the killers' lives matter more," Dow asserted. "Juries chose justice case by case, voters chose it five times, and one outgoing governor is trying to erase it all with a pen. This is a sickening abuse of power."

articles.title: Democrats reach historic House majority not seen since 1992
articles.summary: "House Democrats have just secured the largest majority any party in Congress has held this century. BOOM," Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York sai...
articles.body:
Democrats secured their 258th seat in the House on Sunday, marking the largest majority either party has won in the lower chamber in a general election in three decades.

Democrats have gained 44 House seats so far , four more than the 40 they picked up in President Trump's first midterm in 2018. It's an election sweep unseen since 1992 for either party, creating not only vast opportunities for Democrats to govern but also intense pressure to deliver on campaign promises and priorities .

The 258-seat tally was reached Sunday after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina. Hubbard led Foxx by 330 votes following a recount, according to the North Carolina Board of Elections .

"House Democrats have just secured the largest majority any party in Congress has held this century. BOOM," Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, of New York, wrote on X Sunday afternoon.

The milestone in the 435-member House exceeded Democrats' own expectations, and they could still gain a few more seats with four other House races remaining outstanding: one each in Minnesota and Tennessee and two in Louisiana that are heading to a December runoff.

Republicans will have at least 173 seats in the minority.

The blue wave, or as some have called it, "blue tsunami," sets up a divided government, with the Senate also in Democratic hands and with a Republican president in the White House. Emboldened Democrats are preparing a 100-day agenda to address the high cost of living while also confronting Mr. Trump with a vast oversight agenda for the remainder of his second term.

The Democrats' majority will be bigger than any the party has seen in elections since Bill Clinton was first elected president in 1992 (258) or the election of Barack Obama in 2008 (257), yet not quite the high-water mark of the Franklin D. Roosevelt era, which saw House Democratic majorities swell past 300.

It presents opportunities and challenges ahead.

In an interview on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" on Sunday, Jeffries repeatedly emphasized the need for action, saying, "Can you imagine how angry the American people will be with Washington if, over the next two years, we fail to do anything about affordability, fail to do anything about healthcare, and fail to do anything about immigration?"

Election rout creates a mandate to govern

The numbers underscore the extraordinary scale of Democratic wins, which spanned from the strongest Republican states to the Midwest and East Coast, as voters, angry over high prices and war with Iran and concerned over corruption, made clear their discontent with Mr. Trump.

Persistent negative views of the economy turned against the party in power. Those who said the economy was bad voted for Democrats in their House races, according to CBS News exit polls. This was the second straight election most voters told CBS News inflation was a hardship for them, and more said their finances are worse now compared to two years ago — these voters also backed Democrats over the Republicans for the House.

Taking control of both the House and the Senate come January, the Democrats will carry with them the backing of voters and the expectations to deliver. The Senate Democrats won a 56-seat majority in the 100-member chamber, their biggest advantage in over a decade.

The Democrats, as part of their 100-day agenda, are planning swift votes to reverse the Republicans' Medicaid cuts and restore the Affordable Care Act tax credits the Republicans allowed to expire.

Democrats have vowed to marshal their subpoena powers and launch a flurry of investigations to exert the role of Congress as a check on presidential power. That includes plans to probe how Mr. Trump and his family have become wealthier since he returned to office. Jeffries, who is in line to become House speaker, has not ruled out trying to impeach Mr. Trump for a third time.

"This is a historic moment for our country. This is one of the largest classes we have seen," said progressive leader Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at the Capitol.

The New York Democrat called the big numbers "a mandate for change."

Rep. Tom Suozzi, a centrist Democrat from New York and an accountant by profession, said the House Democrats should focus 75% of their time on affordability issues and 25% on accountability.

"Everything should be tied back to the people — and how it's affecting the people," he said.

For example, he said, as the Democrats launch investigations into Mr. Trump's financial dealings, they should be connecting the dots: "How does that affect people's pocketbooks?"

The White House has issued a warning to Democrats over their planned probes into the administration, going as far as claiming that such investigations — a standard oversight function of Congress — may amount to "blatant criminality."

After House Speaker Mike Johnson struggled to keep the House functioning for the past two years with a narrow single-digit majority — meaning a few GOP lawmakers could derail the agenda — the Democrats will have a wide margin that provides the new leadership much more room to maneuver.

Jeffries, who is poised to make history as the first Black speaker of the House if his colleagues elect him to the job on Jan. 3, 2027, will be able to lose dozens of Democrats on any given vote and still have the 218 needed for passage, in the face of GOP opposition.

"We're not a monolith — people come to the caucus with different ideas — it's OK," said Democratic Rep. Troy Carter of Louisiana, who is expected to lead the Congressional Black Caucus.

Republicans saw their number of House seats fall to one of the lowest tallies in decades. They're far from the end of the Obama administration, when the House Republicans won 247 seats in the 2014 election and the rise of Newt Gingrich when they won 230 seats in 1994.

Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio, who was elected by his colleagues to be the Republican leader in the minority, vowed to fight their way back to power.

"Over the next two years, House Republicans will fight for American families," Jordan said.

The GOP's high-water marks include the 1920 election, with 301 seats for House Republicans.

articles.title: Trump hosts exclusive dinner for investors in his declining meme coin
articles.summary: President Donald Trump will reward top investors in his declining meme coin with an exclusive dinner Sunday night as Democrats focus future congressional pro...
articles.body:
President Donald Trump will reward top investors in his declining meme coin with an exclusive dinner Sunday night as Democrats focus future congressional probes on the president's business dealings, including his crypto ventures.

The event comes as the president's meme coin, known as $TRUMP on crypto exchanges, has declined dramatically in worth since its launch just days before his second inauguration in January 2025. The coin's value peaked at $74 per coin but now trades below $1.

Democrats, gearing up to take control of Congress in the new year, have signaled that the president and his family's crypto ventures will be a target of oversight investigations.

Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., and eight other Democratic senators sent a letter to the White House last month demanding answers about Sunday's meme coin dinner.

"This dinner and scoring mechanism appear carefully constructed to increase investment in $TRUMP, allowing the President to abuse the power of his office to personally enrich himself, as he has throughout this term," the senators wrote.

"President Trump's continued monetization of his name and likeness once again raises serious ethical concerns, necessitating this request for a robust inquiry into the President's financial entanglements and personal profiteering while costs for the American people continue to climb," they added.

Sen. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, and Sen. Richard Blumenthal , D-Conn., the top Democrat on the Senate's Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, were among the letter's signatories. Both senators have been sent letters from the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Texas, Aaron Reitz, warning them against investigating Trump and his associates.

The president's net worth has increased by nearly $3 billion since he returned to office in 2025. More than $1 billion of that has been from cryptocurrencies tied to his family's businesses, while many who invested in those cryptocurrencies experienced steep losses on their investments.

Sunday's dinner will take place at his golf club outside Washington.

The White House referred questions on the event to the company that operates and sells the meme coin, Fight Fight Fight LLC. While the dinner is not listed on the president's public schedule for Sunday, the president often holds off-the-record social gatherings at his properties on the weekends.

The "Most Exclusive Dinner in the World," as it's described on the dinner's website , will feature a number of celebrities, including celebrity businessman Kevin O'Leary, professional boxer Floyd Mayweather and former NBA player Tristan Thompson.

The top 185 holders of the president's coin will earn a seat at the dinner, with the top 29 gaining access to a "special VIP reception." VIP guests will also receive Trump-themed goody bags, and the top four holders with at least 1 million $TRUMP coins are promised 18-karat gold Trump watches. Attendees, however, will not be granted a private meet-and-greet with the president, per the website.

The watchdog group Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington reacted to the dinner on social media on Sunday, writing, "Trump's memecoin dinner today, where likely unvetted $TRUMP memecoin customers will gain special access to Trump, is EXACTLY the reason why we have to ban presidential profiteering."

It's not the first time the president has hosted a dinner for his meme coin investors. In 2025, the top 220 investors of the coin were invited to dine with Trump at his Sterling, Virginia, golf club.

articles.title: Lula exonera ministro para votação do projeto de ajuste na Câmara; medida é temporária | G1
articles.standfirst: José Guimarães deixou secretaria que cuida da articulação do governo no Congresso para reassumir mandato de deputado. Proposta que prevê economia de R$ 50 bilhões em 2027 está na pauta da Câmara.
articles.summary: José Guimarães deixou secretaria que cuida da articulação do governo no Congresso para reassumir mandato de deputado. Proposta que prevê economia de R$ 50 bilhões em 2027 está na pauta da Câmara.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ) exonerou temporariamente o ministro da Secretaria de Relações Institucionais (SRI), José Guimarães, responsável pela articulação política do governo com o Congresso. Assinada na quinta-feira (19), a exoneração foi publicada nesta segunda-feira (23) no "Diário Oficial da União".

A medida tem como objetivo permitir que Guimarães reassuma seu mandato na Câmara dos Deputados e participe das discussões sobre emendas parlamentares e da votação do projeto de ajuste fiscal do Executivo, prevista para esta segunda na Casa .

"A Secretaria de Relações Institucionais da Presidência informa que a exoneração do ministro José Guimarães, publicada no 'Diário Oficial da União', ocorre a pedido e em caráter temporário, para o cumprimento de compromissos parlamentares, na Câmara, relacionados à destinação de emendas e à participação na deliberação sobre o projeto [do ajuste fiscal]", informou a SRI em uma rede social.

Guimarães estava licenciado do mandato desde que assumiu a chefia da pasta no governo Lula . Após a conclusão da votação na Câmara, ele deve retornar ao comando do ministério.

A exoneração faz parte do esforço do Palácio do Planalto para garantir a aprovação célere da proposta de ajuste, que já recebeu aval do Senado na semana passada.

Para evitar que o projeto precise retornar à análise dos senadores, o relator na Câmara, deputado Mauro Benevides Filho (União Brasil-CE), manteve integralmente o texto aprovado no Senado .

O presidente da Câmara, Hugo Motta ( Republicanos -PB), decidiu pautar a matéria nesta segunda-feira, dia em que tradicionalmente não ocorrem votações em plenário, para demonstrar apoio à redução de gastos públicos.

Antes de poderem analisar o conteúdo da proposta, os deputados precisam aprovar um requerimento para que o texto tramite em regime de urgência.

Encabeçado pelo ministro do Planejamento e Orçamento, Bruno Moretti, o pacote busca conter o crescimento das despesas obrigatórias e ampliar a arrecadação federal, com impacto fiscal projetado em R$ 50 bilhões para 2027, segundo estimativa do relator no Senado, Eduardo Braga ( MDB -AM).

No sábado (21), Lula afirmou que a iniciativa não configura uma "reforma", mas sim um "ajuste" necessário para assegurar a "governança sobre o orçamento no ano que vem", reiterando que o governo não fará cortes em programas sociais.

Entre os principais pontos do texto, estão:

teto de 2% para o crescimento real das despesas nos anos em que houver necessidade de contingenciamento;

redução linear de 10% em incentivos e benefícios tributários concedidos a diversos setores da economia;

aval para o Executivo restringir o uso de créditos tributários cruzados, quando empresas usam créditos de um tributo para abater outros impostos, em momentos de contenção de gastos.

José Guimarães e Lula, em imagem de arquivo — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert / PR

articles.title: Após apagões em Cuba, pedidos de refúgio chegam a 4,9 mil no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Solicitações cresceram 34,4% entre julho e setembro, quando atingiram o maior número mensal de 2026. Roraima passou a ser a principal porta de entrada de cubanos no Brasil, superando o Amapá.
articles.summary: Solicitações de cubanos subiram 34,4% entre julho e setembro. Roraima superou o Amapá como principal porta de entrada e concentrou 62,5% dos registros em 2026.
articles.body:
Cubanos saem de Havana, em Cuba, até a Guiana. Para chegar ao Brasil, atravessam fronteiras em botes e atravessam áreas de mata — Foto: Arquivo

Os pedidos de refúgio de cubanos no Brasil chegaram a 4.885 em setembro de 2026, o maior número mensal registrado neste ano, de acordo com o Observatório das Migrações Internacionais (OBMigra), ligado ao Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública . Desde janeiro, as solicitações somam 33.185.

📈 O crescimento dos pedidos ganhou força a partir de agosto, mês em que os pedidos de refúgio chegaram a 4.292, alta de 18% em relação a julho. Em setembro, houve novo avanço, de 13,8%.

🌍 Os dados parciais também mostram uma mudança na principal porta de entrada de cubanos no Brasil. Roraima superou o Amapá , que liderava os registros em 2025, e passou a concentrar 62,5% das entradas nos primeiros nove meses de 2026, segundo a Polícia Federal (veja mais abaixo).

A alta ocorreu em meio ao agravamento da crise econômica e energética em Cuba. Em julho, a ilha enfrentou três apagões nacionais em apenas nove dias . No início de agosto, novos colapsos da rede elétrica deixaram milhões de pessoas sem energia, em um cenário de escassez de combustível, alimentos e medicamentos.

A falta de energia motivou protestos em Havana nos dias seguintes ( leia mais aqui)

No acumulado de janeiro a setembro de 2026, cubanos apresentaram 33.185 pedidos de refúgio, crescimento de 8% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025, quando foram registradas 30.731 solicitações.

🔎 O grupo respondeu por quase 60% de todos os pedidos apresentados no Brasil neste ano.

Até 2024, os venezuelanos lideravam as solicitações de refúgio no país. Naquele ano, foram registrados 27.150 pedidos de venezuelanos e 22.288 de cubanos.

🔄 A situação se inverteu em 2025 , quando os pedidos de cubanos quase dobraram e chegaram a 41.919, enquanto os de venezuelanos recuaram para 21.233.

A mudança se manteve em 2026. Entre janeiro e setembro, enquanto os cubanos fizeram 33,2 mil solicitações, os venezuelanos apresentaram cerca de 9 mil pedidos, uma queda de 43,7% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado.

Infográfico mostra o número de pedidos de refúgio de cubanos no Brasil entre janeiro e setembro de 2025 e 2026 — Foto: Arte/g1

Roraima supera Amapá como principal porta de entrada de cubanos no Brasil

Ávila Basulto, Evelio, Thomas e Eliezer Pantoja, cubanos que vivem em Roraima — Foto: Arquivo

Roraima passou a ser o principal estado de entrada de cubanos no Brasil em 2026, superando o Amapá, que liderava os registros no ano passado.

Como mostrou uma reportagem do g1 Roraima , publicada em junho, cubanos têm utilizado uma rota que passa pela Guiana até chegar a Roraima. Durante a travessia, muitos são aliciados por coiotes, que cobram para facilitar a entrada irregular no Brasil. Os migrantes relataram situações de fome, abandono e exploração financeira ao atravessar rios e áreas de mata.

Dados do Sistema de Tráfego Internacional (STI), da Polícia Federal, mostram que Roraima concentrou 18.501 entradas de cubanos entre janeiro e setembro de 2026, o equivalente a 62,5% de todos os registros no país nesse período. Em todo o ano de 2025, haviam sido contabilizadas 3.702 entradas pelo estado.

👀 O cenário era diferente no ano passado, quando o Amapá liderava os registros, com 8.473 entradas, seguido por São Paulo (4.960) e Roraima (3.702).

➡️ Nos primeiros nove meses de 2026, São Paulo aparece em segundo lugar, com 3.862 entradas, e o Amapá, em terceiro, com 3.183.

A mudança também aparece no tipo de fronteira utilizado. As entradas por vias terrestres passaram de 23% do total registrado em 2025 para 66% nos primeiros nove meses de 2026.

Além da mudança nas portas de entrada, houve crescimento no volume total de deslocamentos. Entre janeiro e setembro de 2026, foram registradas 29.623 entradas de cubanos no Brasil, número 36,8% superior às 21.658 contabilizadas durante os 12 meses de 2025, mesmo com três meses a menos de observação.

No mesmo período de 2026, a Polícia Federal registrou 13.253 saídas de cubanos, resultando em um saldo positivo de 16.370 movimentos de entrada e saída.

🔎 Os dados contabilizam movimentações nas fronteiras, e não necessariamente pessoas que passaram a morar no Brasil. Uma mesma pessoa pode ter mais de uma entrada ou saída.

Quase 100 mil pedidos de cubanos estavam em análise

Cubanos resgatados em Roraima. — Foto: Arquivo

Além das novas solicitações, os dados do OBMigra mostram que 99.306 pedidos de refúgio de cubanos estavam em análise em setembro de 2026. O número corresponde a 58,7% das 169.136 solicitações de todas as nacionalidades que aguardavam etapas de análise ou estavam em recurso.

📌 Os venezuelanos aparecem em segundo lugar, com 36.676 pedidos em análise. Em seguida, estão os colombianos , com 3.440, e os haitianos , com 3.136.

Tabela mostra a quantidade de pedidos de refúgio no Brasil em análise em setembro de 2026 — Foto: Arte/g1

🔎 A quantidade de processos em análise não representa novos pedidos feitos neste ano, mas solicitações registradas anteriormente que ainda não tiveram uma decisão definitiva nas etapas consideradas pela base.

No Brasil, o reconhecimento da condição de refugiado é destinado a pessoas que se enquadram nos critérios previstos na legislação, incluindo situações de perseguição ou grave e generalizada violação de direitos humanos. A apresentação do pedido não significa que o solicitante já tenha obtido o reconhecimento como refugiado.

articles.title: Dólar deve seguir em alta enquanto Lula não indicar nome para Fazenda | G1
articles.summary: Dólar em alta e inflação de 6% preocupam aliados, que defendem a escolha de um nome forte para a Fazenda e cortes de gastos para conter o avanço da dívida pública.
articles.body:
Esse quadro deve se manter até que o petista defina um nome "forte" para o Ministério da Fazenda ou, ao menos, anuncie medidas fiscais mais profundas, com capacidade de estabilizar o crescimento da dívida pública e reduzi-la já no último ano do seu quarto mandato.

Na semana passada, Lula deu novas sinalizações de que não irá seguir o tempo do mercado e vai tomar suas decisões na equipe econômica no seu tempo.

⚠️O risco, alertam aliados do petista, é que, neste caso, o dólar pode ultrapassar R$ 6, pressionando uma inflação que pode chegar a perto de 6%, tornando a administração da política econômica no seu quarto mandato bem mais difícil.

Lula tem dito que terá responsabilidade fiscal, mas que não vai ser refém do mercado . O problema é que o mercado quem financia a dívida pública.

Se os recursos ali aplicados migrarem para investimentos fora do país em ritmo e intensidade acelerados, o dólar vai subir ainda mais.

O cenário seria péssimo para o ano que vem, com inflação em alta, juros no mínimo em 13,75% ao ano e economia desacelerando para a casa de 1% do PIB ou até menos .

Neste caso, Lula será obrigado a fazer um ajuste fiscal mais forte do que gostaria, sob o risco de ter uma tempestade perfeita na economia pela frente.

Por isso, conselheiros tem defendido que ele defina seu ministro da Fazenda ainda em novembro, com a missão de propor medidas fiscais em reduzam o crescimento das despesas obrigatórias .

O mercado tem alertado que o seu cenário da dívida pública não bate com o do governo. A dívida pública em setembro chegou a 82,9% do PIB. No final do ano, pode bater em 83,5% do PIB.

Para a equipe de Lula, em 2030 a dívida se estabilizaria e começaria a cair no ano seguinte. Nas contas de economistas do mercado, ele seguiria subindo, assustando investidores que aplicam seus recursos no Brasil.

articles.title: Ajuste fiscal: Câmara vota projeto com economia de R$ 50 bilhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Relator na Câmara manteve o mesmo texto aprovado pelo Senado para acelerar a votação da proposta e impedir que o projeto precisasse voltar a ser analisado pelos senadores.
articles.summary: O ajuste fiscal do governo Lula prevê corte de 10% em benefícios e restrição a créditos tributários, com votação na Câmara para garantir economia de R$ 50 bilhões.
articles.body:
O presidente da Câmara, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), decidiu acelerar a votação. Normalmente, os deputados não costumam fazer votações às segundas.

O deputado afirma que uma aprovação rápida do ajuste fiscal de Lula deve mandar uma boa sinalização sobre a economia brasileira para o mercado e para a sociedade.

O relator da proposta na Câmara, deputado Mauro Benevides (União Brasil-CE), manteve o mesmo texto aprovado pelos senadores na semana passada. Com isso, o projeto não precisa voltar aos senadores e, se for aprovado pelos deputados, segue para a sanção do presidente Lula.

Com a proposta, o governo federal pretende conter o crescimento das despesas públicas e aumentar a arrecadação. O objetivo, de acordo com o governo, é estabilizar a dívida pública, preservando políticas sociais.

Primeiro, os deputados precisam apreciar um requerimento que permitirá que o projeto seja analisado em regime de urgência pelos deputados. Com ele, o texto pode ser votado direto no plenário, sem cumprir os prazos normais de tramitação.

Depois da passagem pelo Senado, o projeto encabeçado pelo ministro do Planejamento e Orçamento, Bruno Moretti, manteve suas principais medidas. Entre elas, estão:

um limite de 2% para o crescimento de gastos em anos nos quais o contingenciamento for necessário; e

a efetivação de uma defesa antiga do governo: um novo corte linear de 10% em benefícios que o governo dá aos mais diferentes setores da economia.

O relator do texto no Senado Federal, Eduardo Braga (MDB-AM), projetou um impacto nas contas públicas de R$ 50 bilhões em 2027.

Plenário da Câmara dos Deputados — Foto: Divulgação / Câmara dos Deputados

"Na verdade, não houve reforma fiscal, houve um ajuste para que o orçamento da União permita que a gente tenha governança sobre o orçamento no ano que vem. Se a gente não tiver governança, a gente não consegue governar", afirmou Lula sobre a proposta que ainda será analisada pela Câmara.

O presidente voltou a dizer que não fará cortes em programas sociais e fez críticas a agentes do mercado financeiro contrários à política econômica do seu governo.

🔎 Atualmente, empresas que possuem créditos tributários podem deixar de pagar outros impostos, mesmo que sejam de origem diferente dos que deram direito ao crédito.

Pelo projeto, o governo poderá estabelecer restrições a essas compensações, com percentuais diferenciados conforme o valor. A medida poderá ser adotada em momentos nos quais o governo entre em contenção de gastos.

Em manifestações separadas, divulgadas em 12 de novembro, CNI, Fiesp e a Federação das Indústrias do Estado de Minas Gerais (Fiemg) sustentaram que os grandes empresários arcarão com a maior parte do custo do ajuste.

Na prática, a restrição pode aumentar a arrecadação em dinheiro no curto prazo, porque parte dos tributos que seriam pagos com créditos terá de ser efetivamente paga, com dinheiro, pelas empresas.

articles.title: Escala 5x2: AGU diz ao STF que decisão provisória de Dino não é mais necessária após regulamentação do governo | G1
articles.standfirst: AGU diz que manutenção de liminar cria duas regras sobre mesma norma e defende reconhecimento de perda de objeto. Ação que contesta período de transição ainda será julgada pelo plenário da Corte.
articles.summary: AGU diz que manutenção de liminar cria duas regras sobre mesma norma e defende reconhecimento de perda de objeto. Ação que contesta período de transição ainda será julgada pelo plenário da Corte.
articles.body:
A Advocacia Geral da União (AGU) pediu nesta segunda-feira (23) que o Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) reconheça que não é mais necessária a decisão liminar do ministro Flávio Dino que alterou parâmetros da transição para a escala 5x2, depois que o governo editou um decreto regulamentando a emenda aprovada.

A manifestação, assinada pelo advogado-geral da União, Jorge Messias , foi protocolada em uma ação que contesta trechos da proposta aprovada no Congresso e que tratam do período de transição para a redução de jornada.

Há duas semanas, após uma audiência pública realizada com representantes de empregadores e trabalhadores, Dino decidiu alterar, em caráter provisório, alguns parâmetros estabelecidos no texto, entre eles:

escala 5x2, com expedientes diários de até 8 horas e 24 minutos, sem a incidência de adicional de hora extra pelos 24 minutos que ultrapassam as 8 horas habituais;

permissão para que acordos coletivos definam quando serão usufruídas as 8 folgas mensais pelo trabalhador. Antes havia uma trava semanal.

Sessão plenária do STF - 05/11/2026 — Foto: Alejandro Zambrana/STF

Segundo a AGU, a manutenção da decisão liminar criaria duas referências sobre a mesma norma. Além disso, disse que a medida alterou pontos centrais da transição, parâmetros provisórios distintos dos fixados pelo texto promulgado e ainda sujeitos ao julgamento de mérito.

“O reconhecimento da perda de objeto da cautelar pela superveniência do regulamento editado no último 19 de novembro restabelece desde logo a referência única do Texto Constitucional”, argumenta a AGU.

“Nesse contexto, a edição do Decreto nº 13.173/2026 reforça a desnecessidade da medida cautelar. Ao disciplinar a duração do trabalho e o repouso semanal remunerado na forma do texto promulgado, o regulamento promove o saneamento de dúvidas interpretativas antes existentes. Oferece, assim, a empregadores, entidades sindicais e trabalhadores balizas estáveis para a transição, sem a precariedade inerente a uma decisão provisória”, acrescenta.

Dino liberou a ação que vai definir o tema para julgamento de mérito em plenário, mas antes deu prazo para que diferentes órgãos se manifestem. Após essa etapa, caberá ao presidente do STF, ministro Edson Fachin, marcar uma data para o julgamento.

articles.title: Trump's Thanksgiving turkeys arrive at luxury DC hotel as Americans vote on their names
articles.summary: Two turkeys raised on a West Virginia farm strutted a red carpet at the Willard InterContinental Washington, D.C., ahead of Tuesday's pardon.
articles.body: Talk about talking turkey. Two feathered VIPs have checked into one of Washington's most luxurious hotels, complete with plush beds, a red-carpet welcome and a crowd of eager photographers, ahead of President Donald Trump's annual Thanksgiving turkey pardon at the White House. The presidential hopefuls arrived Sunday at the historic Willard InterContinental Washington, D.C., where they were photographed strutting across a red carpet, posing for pictures and standing atop the hotel's beds before their big day on the South Lawn. THE PENNSYLVANIA FARM BEHIND A WHITE HOUSE THANKSGIVING TURKEY TRADITION The U.S. Department of Agriculture celebrated their arrival on X, announcing a "SPECIAL DELIVERY TO WASHINGTON, D.C.!" and describing the birds as "two VERY special guests" receiving the presidential treatment. Photographs shared by the USDA, credited to the White House and National Turkey Federation, showed the plump white birds making their grand entrance before an audience of hotel guests and photographers. One turkey was even pictured riding through the hotel's ornate hallways inside a travel crate perched on a brass luggage cart. The pair appeared equally comfortable with the accommodations, with one bird spreading its feathers atop a neatly made bed while its companion stood nearby. But before the turkeys meet the commander in chief, Americans have been invited to settle a pressing matter of national importance: What should they be called? SOCIAL MEDIA USERS ARE EATING HUGE AMOUNTS OF CARROTS AND SHRIMP FOR A NATURAL TAN The White House launched an online contest offering three possible combinations: "Commander & Chief," "Freedom & Feathers" and "Honey & Ham." Voting on the names closed Sunday at 5 p.m. ET, with the winning pair expected to be announced before a second round of voting opens Monday at 8 a.m. That final vote will determine which turkey receives the official ceremonial pardon. The birds, raised by American turkey farmers Scott and Becky Rightsell at Deans Gap Farm in West Virginia, have already received their own playful presidential biographies. Both hatched July 15, but their tastes apparently differ. According to the White House, one enjoys Golden Delicious apples and scenic country drives, while the other prefers Dr Pepper and dreams of vacationing in Aggieland. The pair was selected from a larger flock based on appearance and temperament, according to West Virginia Gov. Patrick Morrisey's office. Their preparations included getting accustomed to crowds, camera lights and noise. And for Americans who cannot get enough turkey-related excitement, the White House has unveiled "Gobble Getaway," an online game challenging players to help a turkey dodge a chef armed with a net and roasting pan while making its way across the South Lawn to the pardon podium. The annual Thanksgiving tradition dates back to 1947, when the National Turkey Federation first presented a holiday bird to President Harry Truman. Bush established the formal presidential turkey pardon in 1989. Trump and first lady Melania Trump are scheduled to participate in this year's ceremony on Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 2 p.m. ET on the White House South Lawn. Although the public gets to vote on which turkey receives the ceremonial pardon, both birds are traditionally spared the Thanksgiving dinner table. articles.title: John Kennedy on potential 2028 presidential run: ‘If I get really fed up, I could run’
articles.summary: Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) said Sunday he may make a bid for the White House in 2028 if he gets “really fed up.” “My plan, right now, is to run for reelection. I’ve saved up my nickels and dimes. I’ve saved up about $30 million. I’ll add a few nickels to it. And I plan…
articles.body:
Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) said Sunday he may make a bid for the White House in 2028 if he gets “really fed up.”

“My plan, right now, is to run for reelection. I’ve saved up my nickels and dimes. I’ve saved up about $30 million. I’ll add a few nickels to it. And I plan to run for reelection,” Kennedy told NBC News’s Kristen Welker on “Meet the Press.”

“Now, having said that, I’m not going to josh you, Kristen. If I get fed up with things, and catch a wild hare, and have, I don’t know, a spontaneous moment of questionable genius, if I get really fed up, I could run. But it’s not likely,” the Pelican State senator added.

The 2028 election cycle will be the first in more than a decade that will not see President Trump as a candidate given constitutional restrictions. Some members of the GOP who have been floated as possible candidates for the White House in 2028 include Vice President Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

However, if Americans remain as displeased with Trump as they are now, those in his direct orbit may be facing choppy waters if they seek the GOP nomination, and the White House, in two years.

According to a polling average from Decision Desk HQ, Trump’s approval rating was sitting at 37.3 percent as of Sunday night, while his disapproval rating was at 60.4 percent.

Rubio has been gaining steam in discussions around the GOP presidential race, while Vance has been slipping.

Energy has been building around the secretary of State among Republicans as a possible 2028 contender in the wake of Democrats’ expansive midterm gains. The Democrats’ victories have been seen as a rebuke of Trump and have prompted Republicans to wonder whether anyone close to the president can win the White House in two years against a refreshed Democratic Party.

articles.title: A lost Claus: Florida town hit by state’s voter-approved property tax overhaul cancels its Christmas parade
articles.summary: The Grinch didn’t steal Christmas from the residents of Deltona, Florida, but the state’s recently passed Amendment 3 may have.
articles.body: The Grinch didn’t steal Christmas from the residents of Deltona, Florida, but the state’s recently passed Amendment 3 may have. Deltona City Manager Doc Dougherty said in a statement Saturday that the city’s annual Christmas parade would not move forward after nearly 62% of Florida voters backed a proposal that would dramatically slash the amount of taxes homeowners pay. The amendment, which exceeded the 60% voter approval needed to pass, targeted homestead exemptions, which reduce the taxable value of a primary residence when calculating property taxes. The proposal raised the state’s homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 — nearly tripling the current maximum exemption of about $50,000. As a result, homeowners will pay less in taxes, curtailing the funds local jurisdictions receive for their operations. “With the passage of Amendment 3, funding to all cities and counties across the State of Florida is being reduced drastically. It is unfortunate that among all the cities in Central Florida, Deltona will be most affected, which removes millions of dollars’ worth of City services,” Dougherty wrote. He added that the city is expected to cut more than $23 million out of the current budget by 2030, with $12 million of the cuts happening in 2027. Dougherty cited “Deltona’s historic reliance on low property values with little commercial development.” And it’s not just Christmas that’s canceled in Deltona. Dougherty wrote in his statement that all city events moving forward are “effectively canceled,” saying funds would be redirected toward essential services as city officials work to “ensure that Deltona remains a fiscally responsible operation, while trying to meet the needs of our community.” “Working through the financial challenges created by Amendment 3 will take time, and there will be many more difficult decisions ahead,” Dougherty said in his statement. Deltona is located in Volusia County, where registered Republicans outnumber Democrats by nearly 70,000. It is a relatively small city in Florida compared to major hubs like Miami, Orlando or Jacksonville. But even in larger jurisdictions, officials have warned that Amendment 3 will force serious cuts. Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine-Cava said in an interview with the public station WLRN in October that it could cause the county to close parks, fire stations and libraries.

articles.title: Nine million jobs are in limbo, and Congress can fix it before Christmas
articles.summary: If the American Franchise Act doesn't pass before this Congress adjourns, it dies, and the whole process starts over leaving owners in legal limbo.
articles.body: Ask most Americans who owns the McDonald's on the corner, the Holiday Inn off the interstate or the gym down the street, and they'll tell you it's a big corporation. They're wrong. Most of those businesses are owned by local entrepreneurs who put their own savings on the line, sign the lease, make the payroll and live in the town they serve. There are roughly 832,000 of these franchise small businesses in America, and together, they support about 9 million jobs. Yet for more than a decade, Washington hasn't been able to answer a simple question for them: Who is the employer? The answer has flipped with every change in administration. In 2015, the Obama labor board's Browning-Ferris decision blew up decades of precedent and said a parent brand could be on the hook for a franchisee's workers based on "indirect" or even unused control. A 2020 rule restored common sense. In 2023, the Biden board went further than Browning-Ferris, declaring that merely reserving the right to control was enough, before a federal court struck that rule down. The standard has now changed four times since 2015, and another court case could change it again in the next few months. No small-business owner can plan a five-year expansion around a rule that changes every four. CHICK-FIL-A IS ONE OF AMERICA'S TOUGHEST FRANCHISES, AND THE STARTUP COST MAY SHOCK YOU This isn't an abstract legal fight. When the International Franchise Association and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce studied the damage from the expanded standard, they found it cost the economy $33.3 billion a year, led to as many as 376,000 fewer job opportunities and drove a 93% increase in lawsuits against franchise businesses. Ninety-two percent of the brands and owners surveyed said the rule meant less support from their brand. That last number is the one that should bother Congress most. Under a sprawling joint-employer test, every bit of help a franchisor gives — a training program, an HR template, a workplace-safety manual — becomes evidence that it is really the boss. So the brands pull back. The national company with the lawyers and the compliance staff protects itself. The owner of three sandwich shops is left on her own. A rule sold as protecting workers ends up kneecapping the small employers who hire them. The fix is sitting in front of Congress right now. The American Franchise Act (H.R. 5267 / S. 3525) writes one permanent, franchise-specific standard into federal law under both the National Labor Relations Act and the Fair Labor Standards Act. A franchisor would be a joint employer only if it both possesses and exercises substantial, direct and immediate control over essential terms of employment like wages, hiring and scheduling. Setting brand standards, offering training or requiring safety qualifications would not, by themselves, make a franchisor the employer. That is how franchising worked for most of its history, and it is how it should work. Most important, it would be the law — not a board decision that the next administration can toss out on a party-line vote. This is that rarest of things in Washington: a genuinely bipartisan bill. It was introduced by seven Republicans and seven Democrats. It has 158 cosponsors in the House, cleared the House Education and Workforce Committee in July and has the backing of the White House. Members like Rep. Kevin Hern of Oklahoma, who owned and operated McDonald's restaurants before he came to Congress, understand from the inside what it means to meet a payroll under rules that won't sit still. REP ROGER WILLIAMS: 250 YEARS OF HARD WORK PAYS OFF FOR MAIN STREET BUSINESSES At Unleash Prosperity Now, our new paper, "Nine Million Jobs at Stake: Why Franchising Needs Regulatory Certainty," lays out what's on the line. One in eight American businesses with at least one employee is a franchise, and nearly two-thirds of local franchise owners are first-time business owners. This year alone, franchising is projected to create more than 150,000 new jobs. The conclusion is plain: Clarity is the cheapest pro-growth policy Congress can pass. It would also lift a compliance headache off small-business owners and free them to keep prices down at a moment when Americans have made clear that affordability is what they care about most. It doesn't cost the Treasury a dime, and it lets hundreds of thousands of small employers get back to hiring. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION The clock matters. If the American Franchise Act doesn't pass before this Congress adjourns, it dies, and the whole process starts over, with a future labor board free to swing the pendulum back again. Franchise owners have already spent 10 years in limbo. They shouldn't be made to wait for another election cycle. Pass the American Franchise Act. CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM STEVE MOORE

articles.title: Democrats plan 12 presidential debates, with first in June
articles.summary: Democrats are planning 12 presidential primary debates for the 2028 cycle, with the first set for June 2027. In a Monday press release obtained by The Hill’s sister network NewsNation, the Democratic National Committee (DNC) said 12 primary debates are set to occur during the cycle. Five of those debates will occur next year, and…
articles.body:
Democrats are planning 12 presidential primary debates for the 2028 cycle, with the first set for June 2027.

In a Monday press release obtained by The Hill’s sister network NewsNation, the Democratic National Committee (DNC) said 12 primary debates are set to occur during the cycle. Five of those debates will occur next year, and the other seven will happen in the election year.

The DNC said the debates will kick off next June, with another debate the following month and the final debate happening in March 2028. However, the DNC also said it “reserves the right to adjust the schedule as necessary. “

“Democrats are on offense after our historic victories in the midterms, and the DNC is keeping our foot on the gas as we head into the 2028 cycle,” DNC Chair Ken Martin said in a statement.

“The fair and transparent process and experienced leadership team we’re announcing today will keep our party united, strengthen our eventual nominee, and put Democrats in position to take back the White House,” he added.

In the press release, the DNC said it will unveil details like locations and media partners for the first two debates in January. And if a considerable number of candidates run in the primary, “early debates may occur over two consecutive nights.”

The committee planning the debates is set to be headed up by Minyon Moore, the DNC’s senior adviser for debates, and DNC Executive Director Roger Lau, with other members of the committee being made up of advisers and staff from prior Democratic presidential campaigns.

“I’m honored to be guiding the team that will run the 2028 Democratic Presidential Primary Debate process. I’m committed to ensuring our debate process is not only fair and transparent, but that it also sets our nominee up for success in the general election,” Moore said in a statement.

Per the DNC, candidates can earn debate eligibility similarly to the 2020 debate process, through pathways like their standing in polling and grassroots funding, and the exact pathways to qualify for the June and July 2027 debates are set to be unveiled next January. However, the Democratic presidential candidates must also “sign and follow the DNC’s Fair Campaign Practices Pledge committing to denounce dark money spending in our primary in order to qualify for debate participation.”

A DNC official told NewsNation that Democrats like Rep. Greg Casar (D-Texas), Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and Sen. Andy Kim (D-N.J.) support the pledge.

The Democrats are also set to feature “influencers and creators” in their debate system for the 2028 cycle in order to boost viewership.

articles.title: Democratic National Committee sets broad rules for the party’s 2028 presidential debates
articles.summary: The Democratic National Committee will hold 12 debates next year and in 2028 for candidates seeking the party’s presidential nomination, the party announced, as it sets rules of the road for what’s expected to be a crowded campaign for the White House.
articles.body: The Democratic National Committee will hold 12 debates next year and in 2028 for candidates seeking the party’s presidential nomination, the party announced, as it sets rules of the road for what’s expected to be a crowded campaign for the White House. The Monday morning announcement from the DNC lays out a process that hews closely to the rules under which Democrats ran in 2020, the last time the party had an open primary. Each debate may be split across two nights, with no more than 20 candidates qualifying in total — an implicit acknowledgment of the dozens of Democrats from all corners of the party who are openly musing about running for president. And the party will determine who makes the debate stage through criteria such as polling and grassroots fundraising figures. Exact dates and media partners for the first two debates will be announced in January. The biggest rules change compared to past campaigns is that the party will require presidential candidates to sign a pledge denouncing “dark money spending in our primary” used to boost a candidate or cut down a Democratic rival. It’s a relatively symbolic pledge — it doesn’t have the teeth to actually stop that kind of outside spending, but it will try to attach a political cost to it, all while uniting Democratic candidates behind the party’s frustration with rampant outside spending in federal elections. Candidates will also have to adhere to a series of other promises, as always. That includes agreeing to follow the DNC’s new nominating calendar. Candidates who compete in states that are trying to jump ahead of the party’s approved early-primary order face being stripped of delegates won in every early-nominating state, and the DNC made that punishment harder to undo than in past years. Minyon Moore, a longtime DNC senior adviser and veteran party strategist, will lead the its debate planning committee alongside Roger Lau, the party’s executive director. The DNC added that the committee also includes people who staffed past presidential campaigns including those of Kamala Harris, Joe Biden, Bernie Sanders, Elizabeth Warren, Amy Klobuchar, Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama. “Democrats are on offense after our historic victories in the midterms, and the DNC is keeping our foot on the gas as we head into the 2028 cycle,” DNC Chair Ken Martin said in a statement. “The fair and transparent process and experienced leadership team we’re announcing today will keep our party united, strengthen our eventual nominee, and put Democrats in position to take back the White House.” The June start to the debate calendar puts the Democrats in line with their 2020 schedule, when NBC News hosted the first debates in Miami alongside MSNBC and Telemundo. Those events sparked the first in-person clashes among the sprawling field of Democratic hopefuls, with two 10-person debates on back-to-back days. Then, the vast majority of the announced Democratic candidates qualified for the stage. Like in 2020, the DNC plans to randomize the two-night debate stages “in a manner that will ensure parity across both nights.” The announcement also includes additional details about some of the more technical rules governing the nominating contest. Under the party’s new pledge against dark money, candidates have to agree to a blanket denunciation of political nonprofits that don’t disclose their donors or super PACs that spend for or against candidates in the primary race, and they must specifically denounce new outside spending that pops up on their behalf. A DNC official told NBC that the pledge has been endorsed by a handful of elected Democrats, including Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Andy Kim, of Massachusetts and New Jersey respectively, as well as Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt. Candidates must also agree not to enter into any joint fundraising agreement with local party organizations unless they’re the party’s official nominee, a measure aimed at ensuring the Democratic Party apparatus remains neutral across different levels.
