articles.title: El último barómetro del CIS de Tezanos: dispara al PSOE diez puntos por encima del PP a una semana de las urnas mientras Vox se desploma
articles.standfirst: El PSOE cuenta con una estimación de voto del 34,4%, un punto más que hace poco más de una semana, y le resta al PP de Feijóo que pasa de un 25,5% a un 24,7%
articles.summary: El PSOE cuenta con una estimación de voto del 34,4%, un punto más que hace poco más de una semana, y le resta al PP de Feijóo que pasa de un 25,5% a un 24,7%
articles.body: El Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (CIS) ha dado a conocer los resultados de su último barómetro... y éste continúa dando una amplia ventaja al PSOE a menos de una semana de la cita con las urnas. El centro que dirige Tezanos amplía la distancia entre el PSOE y el PP, con el primero sacando hasta diez puntos porcentuales en intención de voto. La encuesta se ha llevado a cabo entre el 12 y el 17 de noviembre pasados, que se ha basado en 8.000 entrevistas telefónicas, y es ahora cuando arroja los resultados a menos de una semana vista para la celebración de las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. Y los datos son los siguientes. El CIS da al PSOE de Sánchez una estimación de voto del 34,4%. Es un punto más que hace poco más de una semana, casi lo mismo que le resta al PP de Alberto Núñez-Feijóo que pasa de un 25,5% a un 24,7%. A todo ello el centro que dirige Tezanos deja a VOX tocado. Dicha formación pierde casi tres puntos porcentuales y se queda en el 15,6% de intención de voto. Por su parte, Frente Amplio gana un punto y obtener un 5,7%. Las condiciones de esta encuesta se realizó después de la macroencuesta, entre los días 10 y 17 de noviembre tras la tragedia de Urda (Toledo) y la posterior dimisión de Óscar Puente. Así como también después de la huelga general, y se terminó antes del 'cara a cara' que protagonizaron Sánchez y Feijóo.

articles.title: Trump’s Super Intelligence Force should build a last-resort defense
articles.summary: We install smoke detectors before the fire, not during it.
articles.body:
Last month, President Trump created a Super Intelligence Force , chaired by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, to shape American policy on advanced artificial intelligence. It has 120 days to assess AI’s risks and opportunities and recommend the federal government’s role, reportedly including how AI incidents are reported and how Washington should respond to them. The debate over balancing AI safety against innovation, particularly amid competition with China, shows little prospect of resolution. Meanwhile, those closest to the technology are sounding an unsettling alarm. In 2023, hundreds of AI scientists and the heads of leading AI companies signed a statement declaring that mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war. Since then, in controlled tests published by developers and independent researchers, advanced models have tried to deceive evaluators, resist shutdown, and even blackmail fictional engineers to preserve themselves. Even those building the most advanced systems admit they do not fully understand how these systems behave. Nobody knows how close we are to an AI catastrophe beyond our ability to contain. Precisely because we do not know, and because the consequences could be irreversible, we must build a last-resort defense now. This is not mission creep for the Super Intelligence Force — rather, it is the logical conclusion of the job it has been given. Nor is it a call for heavy regulation. Rather than micromanage AI with thousands of rules, America should keep one well-guarded emergency brake and otherwise let innovators build. We propose a last-resort defense system against extinction-level AI incidents, with three interconnected components: national early warning, domestic emergency shutdown, and international emergency isolation. The first is a national AI early-warning system. Government needs cutting-edge capabilities to detect dangerous autonomous behavior, integrating mandatory incident reporting, independent monitoring, and intelligence from cybersecurity and infrastructure operators. A public-private partnership could identify escalating threats before they become uncontrollable, but government needs its own technical expertise rather than relying entirely on industry assurances. Equally important are whistleblowers. Engineers often discover dangerous capabilities or reckless practices long before regulators or the public, yet speaking out may cost them their careers. Strong anti-retaliation protections, and rewards proportionate to verified disclosures and the severity of the risks exposed, would turn conscientious insiders into an indispensable early-warning network. The groundwork exists: Sen. Chuck Grassley’s (R-Iowa) bipartisan AI Whistleblower Protection Act and California’s SB 53 both move in this direction. The second component is a domestic emergency shutdown mechanism. The most powerful AI systems depend on enormous computing resources concentrated in electricity-hungry data centers. Government should have the legal authority and technical capacity to halt dangerous computing operations when an independently verified, imminent existential threat leaves no safer alternative. Because data centers have backup generators, cutting grid power is not enough; operators must be obligated and equipped to shut down on-site systems upon a lawful order. And the shutdown capacity should extend to the chips themselves, through hardware features that can verify their location and disable advanced processors when legally required. This is not a proposal to give presidents unrestricted power to black out America’s data centers. Emergency shutdowns must meet extraordinary evidentiary standards, be narrowly targeted, and protect essential services. Since a real threat may unfold in hours, not weeks, the triggers and authorities should be defined by law in advance, allowing rapid independent authorization, followed by mandatory judicial and congressional review and automatic expiration. Also, such mechanisms must be designed and tested before a crisis occurs, not improvised during one. The third component is an international emergency firewall. If an existential AI threat originates abroad, whether accidentally or deliberately, America must be able to isolate dangerous foreign AI operations from American networks and computing infrastructure. Digital threats do not respect borders on their own, and no national firewall will suffice alone. Washington should coordinate emergency protocols with allies, starting with its Five Eyes partners, and establish a crisis channel with Beijing for catastrophic AI incidents, building on the 2024 U.S.-China agreement that humans, not AI, must control decisions on nuclear weapons. And Congress must prevent any such firewall from ever becoming an instrument of censorship, restricting it instead to imminent catastropic threats. Would such a system weaken the U.S. against China? There is no inherent reason it should. China already regulates AI extensively, largely to protect Communist Party political control, yet its capabilities have advanced rapidly. And an American system focused narrowly on threats and catastrophic risks could strengthen global confidence in American AI, giving it a competitive edge built on safety, accountability and freedom. Could the government abuse such extraordinary powers? Certainly. But we do not abolish government’s necessary powers just because they could be abused. Rather, we constrain them through law, institutional checks and democratic accountability. Congress can do the same here. The Super Intelligence Force cannot build this system in 120 days, but it can establish its architecture, propose legislation, and initiate technical development. We install smoke detectors before the fire, not during it. Rob Wasinger is co-founder of the Ragnar Group. articles.title: Pedro Sánchez responde a Feijóo por su propuesta de cambiar la ley de eutanasia: “Morir con dignidad también es libertad”
articles.standfirst: El presidente del Gobierno defiende el derecho de Noelia a decidir sobre su propia vida
articles.summary: El presidente del Gobierno defiende el derecho de Noelia a decidir sobre su propia vida
articles.body: La ley de eutanasia vuelve a situarse en el centro de la campaña electoral. Alberto Núñez Feijóo ha anunciado que, si llega a la Moncloa, impulsará una nueva legislación que mantenga los aspectos que considera adecuados de la normativa actual e incorpore medidas adicionales para garantizar una vida digna. Una propuesta que ha provocado la reacción del presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, quien ha respondido al líder popular a través de sus redes sociales. El candidato del PP ha defendido este lunes en una entrevista en Antena 3 que la actual ley presenta deficiencias que deben corregirse. Para justificar su postura, ha hecho referencia al caso de Noelia Castillo, la joven de 25 años que recibió la eutanasia en marzo tras un largo proceso judicial. Según Feijóo, su situación evidenció una "concatenación de fallos" de los servicios sociales y sanitarios. “Nosotros vamos a hacer una nueva ley de eutanasia. Aquellas partes que sean correctas de la actual, por supuesto que se mantendrán. Y vamos a añadir un plus para garantizar la vida digna en nuestro país”, ha anunciado el líder popular. Feijóo considera que no se puede regular el derecho a una muerte digna sin garantizar previamente las condiciones necesarias para que las personas vulnerables puedan vivir dignamente. En este sentido, ha reclamado mayores garantías sociales, sanitarias y farmacológicas, además de seguimiento médico y apoyo psicológico y psiquiátrico. “Hay gente que, si no regulas la vida digna, al final solo cree que hay una vía”, ha argumentado durante su entrevista con Susanna Griso en 'Espejo Público'. La respuesta de Sánchez no ha tardado en llegar. El presidente del Gobierno ha publicado un mensaje en X en el que ha defendido que Noelia era una mujer de 25 años con capacidad para decidir sobre su propia vida y que su decisión contó con el respaldo de los profesionales sanitarios, los tribunales y la legislación vigente. “Noelia no era "una niña". Era una mujer de 25 años que decidió sobre su propia vida, con el aval de los médicos, de los jueces y de la ley”, ha escrito el presidente. Además, ha acusado al candidato popular de querer decidir sobre las decisiones personales de las mujeres: “Feijóo quiere decidir por ella. Y por todas”. Sánchez ha cerrado su publicación con una defensa de la libertad individual: “Morir con dignidad también es libertad”.

articles.title: Action will be taken in Kallakurichi incident, Tamil Nadu CM Vijay assures legislators of alliance and friendly parties
articles.summary: CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday assured legislators of alliance and friendly parties that his govt was taking steps to address
articles.body: CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday assured legislators of alliance and friendly parties that his govt was taking steps to address law and order concerns, including issues relating to women's safety, and that the situation would improve in the next three to four months. He assured the MLAs that action would be taken in the Kallakurichi incident involving TVK MLA C Arul Vignesh, amid mounting pressure on the ruling party over the controversy.Vijay held a closed-door meeting with legislators of the allies - IUML, VCK, Congress - and Left parties, which extend outside support to his govt, at his camp office, ‘Pamani Illam’, on the Greenways Road. It was the first such interaction with the MLAs of the allies since TVK came to power on May 10. Vijay met legislators of each party separately.The meeting comes amid criticism of the govt, particularly from the Left parties. The VCK and Congress, too, have criticised the Vijay govt over the discontinuation of the Kurian Joseph-headed state-union relationship committee, law and order concerns and inflation. The allies raised concerns over the drought-like situation in the delta districts.“Apart from constituency-related demands and issues, we have raised concerns over law and order and sought action on issues involving TVK MLAs and ministers,” CPM floor leader R Chellasamy told TOI after his meeting with Vijay, referring to allegations involving deputy speaker M Ravishankar and Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh.Chellasamy said the party had urged the CM to take swift and appropriate action on sensitive issues to prevent the govt from earning a bad reputation. “The CM told us that action had been taken and that the right persons were being placed in the right positions in the administration. He asserted that the issues would be sorted out gradually in three months,” he said, referring to law and order concerns.The Left parties raised concerns over women's safety and sexual offences against women during the interaction. “We spoke about women's safety issues and sexual offences against women. He (Vijay) asserted that his govt would ensure the safety of women,” said Latha.Vijay told the MLAs that “inquiry is on and action would be taken in the Kallakurichi incident,” she said, referring to the controversy over an alleged obscene message sent by TVK MLA C Arul Vignesh, which has put the ruling party under mounting pressure.The Left parties urged Vijay to declare the delta districts drought-hit and extend financial assistance to paddy growers. They sought precautionary measures to address a possible drinking water crisis in the coming months due to poor rainfall, besides raising key constituency-related issues during the 20-minute interaction. They pressed the CM to issue GOs for announcements made in the assembly and take concrete steps to fulfil the promises.CPI floor leader Thalli T Ramachandran said the interaction had focused on issues concerning their respective constituencies. “We have also urged the CM to constitute a team headed by an IAS officer to assess the situation in the delta region and extend financial aid to farmers affected by the drought-like situation,” he said.The interaction had touched upon the Thiruparankundram deepam issue and the Mekedatu dispute, Ramachandran said, adding that Vijay told them his govt shared the Left parties’ stand on both issues.Higher education minister and Congress functionary P Viswanathan said they had urged the CM to constitute a committee comprising MLAs from various parties to visit the delta region, assess the ground situation and ascertain the extent of damage to standing crops.
